item.description: Cults gonna' cult. Massachusetts just made sure a January 6 rioter who punched a cop won't be practicing medicine in the state again. Good! The state Board of Registration in Medicine issued a Final Decision and Order on July 16 permanently revoking Dr. Jacquelyn Starer's right to renew her license, citing her role storming the Capitol and striking a Metropolitan Police officer with her closed fist while cursing at her. Starer, a longtime Ashland obstetrician-gynecologist with a subspecialty in addiction medicine, pleaded guilty to eight federal counts including two felonies and was sentenced to nine months behind bars. trump pardoned her not long into his second term, wiping away the consequences of a violent attack on law enforcement that she herself admitted to. But luckily that pardon didn't touch her medical license though, and the Massachusetts board wasn't having any of it. Even the officer she assaulted spoke up at sentencing, telling the court she feared for her life defending the Capitol that day. It's a small but meaningful reminder that a presidential pardon can erase a criminal record, but it can't force a state licensing board to pretend nothing happened. Starer's attorneys said losing her ability to practice has left a big hole in her life. item.title: Trump Administration Admits Canceling Grants to States That Did Not Vote for Him
item.description: When the Trump administration canceled more than $7.5 billion in Biden-era federal grants for clean energy projects in October, it framed the move as an urgent corrective to protect taxpayer funds from waste. But it wasn’t true. In little-noticed court documents, federal officials acknowledged this month that they had terminated the funding “based solely” on political criteria, targeting projects in states that were represented by Democrats and had voted for Kamala Harris, the party’s presidential nominee, in the 2024 election. The stunning admission offered an unvarnished glimpse into the way President Trump has weaponized the provision of federal education, energy, health, housing and infrastructure aid in his second term. Far from rooting out the sort of misspending that Mr. Trump sees as rife in Washington, the White House has instead sought to leverage the budget as a tool to assist its allies — or as a cudgel to hurt the president’s foes. The saga illustrates the stakes as the Trump administration is completing a set of rules that would provide the president even greater control over more than $1 trillion in annual federal grants. To critics, the new regulation would only make it easier for Mr. Trump to strike wider tranches of congressionally approved funding over political differences. “The risk that the Trump administration is willing to go to extreme lengths to politicize grant-making is not a hypothetical,” said Devin O’Connor, a senior fellow at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, a left-leaning group. He previously served in the Biden administration. “If they are willing to be that blatant about it,” Mr. O’Connor said of the court filing, “then I think we should take seriously when they put forward a framework that would allow for the extreme politicization of grant-making across all of the federal government.” The White House and the Energy Department did not respond to requests for comment. The administration’s latest concession about the grants came in a lawsuit filed by a group of California researchers challenging various federal agencies that have canceled Biden-era funding. After reviewing its spending, the Energy Department last fall created a list that recommended canceling more than 600 grants awarded by the Biden administration for a wide range of novel energy projects. That list included funding for projects in states represented by both Republicans and Democrats. But in October, the White House budget office, led by Russell T. Vought, terminated only 284 of those grants. In a social media post announcing the news, Mr. Vought pointed to the motivations: “Nearly $8 billion in Green New Scam funding to fuel the Left’s climate agenda is being canceled,” he said. Months later, in court filings, federal officials indicated there was little else that had informed the final decision about which grants to cancel. “With one exception,” a lawyer for the Energy Department conceded in a court filing this month, “the 284 terminated grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to Kamala Harris in the 2024 election and has two Democratic-caucusing senators.” The lawyer acknowledged that none of the grants were included in the October terminations “based on any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction or performance-based factor.” In contrast, the administration left untouched hundreds of additional energy grants in states that were represented by Republicans and had backed Mr. Trump in the last election, even though the Energy Department had recommended canceling them, the government confirmed in the July court filing. Source: https://electionlawblog.org/?p=157593

item.title: OP delivered. Fight me.
item.description: EDITED: Hey guys. I said I'd share the whole thing and here it is. (background at the bottom if you're new!) github.com/812theory/812 All 8 episodes. Every draft. Every background doc. The pitch materials. The coverage that called it unpitchable. The mess I made before I figured out what I was making. It's all there, nothing hidden. I genuinely hope it helps at least one writer who's earlier in their journey than they want to be. That's the whole point. Now... if you thought any of this was AI, go read the mess. Then come fight me. For people who are new: In 2019 I posted a short story to r/HFY called "I Am Not a God." https://www.reddit.com/r/HFY/comments/egluod/i_am_not_a_god_oc/ A man in a bungalow in Bangkok. People bent reality around him without realizing it. He didn't notice because he'd been alive for centuries and his brain had built a wall around everything he couldn't process. No genre, no plan, just a character I couldn't stop thinking about. That post went nowhere. I filed it away. Seven years later I pulled it back out. By then I'd sold scripts to Netflix and worked on Strange New Worlds for 3.5 seasons. I'd also spent three months in an ICU and three months in addiction treatment. Turns out the character had been waiting for me to become the person who could actually write him. In about two weeks it became an 8-episode limited series. Something is eating Bangkok, not destroying it, organizing it. The 7-11 door chime is the first thing that goes. A structural engineer who's been alive for centuries walks the same route every morning at 8:12 AM and genuinely doesn't notice that traffic stops for him. Some of you saw me posting about the process while I was in it. Then I finished it. And I said I'd share the whole thing when I did. So here it is. The show, every draft, every background doc, the pitch bible that got called unpitchable, thirteen production rules, the Reddit post that started everything in 2019, and the thinking behind every choice. Open source. Take it, learn from it, steal the good parts. github.com/812theory/812 EDIT: 4pm EST: I captured five moments from this comment thread that broke something open — about the work, about the audience, about what it even means to open source a TV show. What happened when the work met the world: https://github.com/812theory/812/blob/main/the-making/launch-feedback.md

item.title: GovBrief Today #540
item.description: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said politics never decided which grants got canceled, and his own lawyers just told a court it was the only thing that did. They agreed in writing on Friday that all but one of the 284 canceled grants, $7.5 billion worth, went to a state Kamala Harris won, and that nothing about cost or performance went into picking them. A judge already ruled against them twice this year, pointing out that comparable projects in states Trump won were left running. Wright called the accusation bullshit in front of the House Science Committee last month and promised to keep saying so a million times. The Energy Department spent Friday insisting the filing was about the timing of an announcement. They denied it everywhere except in court. item.description: Pippa the golden retriever lives in Brisbane, Australia. Every day, she runs to the front gate to collect the mail and bring it to her owners. It's one of her favorite things to do. Her postman, Martin Studer, noticed how excited she gets. So on days when there are no letters, he writes her one himself. On the delivery slip, he writes "Mail For Pippa," sometimes adding a smiley face or a heart. Martin told the BBC, "I just didn't want to let her down." His small act of kindness has made Pippa's day—and brought a smile to the rest of the world too...
